correction: PR #1531: Adding the delegated training view and tests to their Xcode targets changed the project manifest without refreshing its exact diagnostic dependency pin, failing Mac Runner Routing Tests.
mechanization: Retain the existing seven exact dependency pins and refresh only the reviewed project manifest hash. The required Mac Runner Routing Tests compare each pin to current source bytes and exercise the trusted CLI against accepted tooling and rejected changed, missing, symlinked, dirty and untracked inputs. The existing regression failed before the pin update and passes afterward.

codebase.rationale: A runtime application change cannot keep a separately reviewed workflow dependency pin synchronized; deriving the pin from candidate bytes would remove the trust boundary.

static.rationale: The existing required runner-routing regression compares the seven pinned digests to actual source bytes and verifies trusted CLI admission and refusal without executing candidate tooling.

correction: LYB-231: StoreKit purchase-and-restore tests created and released a new SKTestSession per test, so a previous session's asynchronous teardown could erase the next test's purchase (run 40011070495: purchase verified, then restore found no subscriptions). Use one process-wide session and wait for a verifiably clean StoreKit state before each test.
mechanization: StoreKitPurchaseRestoreTests creates the SKTestSession once through a single accessor and resets it in setUp behind a bounded clean-state gate (no transactions, no entitlements), without changing any lifecycle assertion. The required iOS StoreKit job runs it on every iOS change and on main, and the job script names the failure signature on any recurrence.

codebase.rationale: One private accessor owns the only SKTestSession and every lifecycle test obtains it through that accessor, so the per-test create-and-release pattern that raced StoreKit teardown no longer exists in the test target.

static.rationale: The existing no_print_statements custom rule, executed by required strict SwiftLint, rejects the offending calls without changing test assertions or gate configuration.
